synopsis: Bekker-Wong is presented as a semi-empirical terramechanics approach for predicting braking force and sinkage on soft soil [f6096, f6461]. The underlying terramechanics findings say tractive and braking forces depend on soil type, contact area, load and slip, and that tracks retain more shear force than tires in soft soil [f6006, f6007]. Across the virtual-job-site and brake-timing chapters, Project Chrono provides an implementation route: its terrain options include a Soil Contact Model using Bekker-Wong pressure-sinkage and shear parameters, alongside rigid terrain and more expensive granular or deformable approaches [f3739, f6014]. The supplied facts identify modeling options and physical dependencies, but provide no numerical braking results or validation accuracy for these models [f6006, f6014, f6461].

relations.note: Details Chrono’s terrain options and how Bekker-Wong parameters enter its Soil Contact Model.
